bootstrap.notes: 03-modeling's own handoff.json was read directly with full confidence (sha256 verified below) - but the immediately-preceding stage in the numbered chain, 04-deep-learning, has no handoff.json at all, since its dl_gate verdict (not_warranted) was correctly never overridden and the stage never ran. Per the kernel's bootstrap protocol, a missing immediate predecessor makes this stage's overall bootstrap 'reconstructed', not 'handoff', even though the actual model_result/problem_spec this stage depends on came from a real, unbroken handoff one stage further back.

decisions.decision: Serve the model behind a small internal-only FastAPI service (predictor/), reached by the dhaka-kacchi-connect admin backend over the docker-compose network, never exposed to the internet.
decisions.rationale: Confirmed with the user directly (AskUserQuestion) over two alternatives: batch/offline-only (rejected - the user explicitly wants a live 'type a caption, get a flag' UI experience) and porting the model into Node/JS (rejected - couples retraining to a manual code port and risks training-serving skew). A tiny internal service keeps Python-model logic in Python, cleanly separated from the Node backend, and matches this repo's own deploy/CLAUDE.md 'Adding a future second backend' pattern exactly.

decisions.decision: The shipped artifact is refit on ALL 360 labeled rows (train + the now-spent test split), using the exact hyperparameters (C=2.6366...) chosen in stage 03 - no re-tuning.
decisions.rationale: The test split's job (an honest, single, final evaluation) is done; refitting on more data before shipping is standard practice and does not re-use the test set for any decision - only the already-fixed hyperparameters are reused, so this is not a second use of the test set for model selection.

decisions.decision: ml/03-modeling/features.py is copied verbatim into the served image at Docker build time (predictor/Dockerfile's COPY line), not reimplemented in the service.
decisions.rationale: This is the kernel's 'one code path' defense against training-serving skew, in the simplest form available without a shared package registry: the exact same file, not a hand-ported equivalent. A parity test (running the same input through both paths) was not built as a separate CI check - see risks.

decisions.decision: The service refuses to load model.joblib if its SHA-256 doesn't match model.sha256 (written alongside it at training time), verified explicitly in predictor/app/model.py before build_artifact.py's own joblib.load() ever runs.
decisions.rationale: joblib.load wraps pickle - loading the artifact executes arbitrary code. Per the kernel's own security section, an artifact this class of executable needs the same provenance-check discipline as a code deploy: hash recorded at build, verified at load, refuse on mismatch rather than degrade silently.

decisions.decision: Per-request 'why' is computed as coefficient x encoded-feature-value for the top 5 by magnitude, not SHAP or a separate explainability library.
decisions.rationale: Only valid because the winning model is linear (logistic regression) - this method would not generalize to a tree model. Chosen because it's exact (not an approximation like SHAP would need to be for a black-box model) and needs no extra dependency, matching problem_spec.constraints.explainability_required=true cheaply.

decisions.decision: Deployed directly (rollout.strategy=direct), no shadow run or canary period.
decisions.rationale: Single internal operator, advisory-only output with no automated effect, a few predictions a day at most. The blast radius of a bad prediction is one person second-guessing one social post - shadow/canary infrastructure would cost more to build and maintain than the risk being protected against justifies at this scale.

decisions.decision: retraining.trigger=manual, no scheduled or drift-triggered retraining pipeline built.
decisions.rationale: At ~15-20 new posts a month combined across both platforms, automatic retraining would fire on almost no new data each time and mostly re-confirm the same 360-row fit. Re-running ml/01 through ml/03/05 by hand once post volume has grown meaningfully (see dl_gate.revisit_if in 03-modeling) is the right cadence for a project this size.

decisions.decision: Structured JSON logging (request id, model version, platform, label, probability, latency) to stdout only - no dashboard, no drift detection job, no alerting built this pass.
decisions.rationale: Honest scope-matching: a full monitoring stack (PSI/KS drift checks, alerting) is disproportionate to a single-operator, few-predictions-a-day internal tool. Logs are the real, inspectable record if something looks wrong; automated monitoring is a stated gap, not a silent one - see risks.

assertions.claim: The threshold served (0.49) is read from stage 03's model_metadata.json, not hardcoded separately or left at the sklearn default of 0.5.
assertions.method: ml/05-production/build_artifact.py reads chosen_threshold from ml/03-modeling/artifacts/results.json and writes it into model_metadata.json; predictor/app/model.py reads threshold from that same metadata file at load time.
assertions.evidence: model_metadata.json's threshold field = 0.49, confirmed via a live /v1/predict call returning threshold: 0.49 in the response.

assertions.claim: The object served is the actual fitted sklearn Pipeline (preprocessing + classifier together), not a hand-reimplemented scoring function.
assertions.method: build_artifact.py serializes the whole Pipeline (ColumnTransformer + LogisticRegression) via joblib.dump; predictor/app/model.py loads it via joblib.load and calls .predict_proba() on it directly.

assertions.claim: A parity test comparing offline (training-time) and online (serving-time) feature values for the same input.
assertions.method: Not built as an automated CI check. Manual parity was exercised instead: the exact same features.py file is copied byte-for-byte into the served image (see decision training-serving-parity-via-file-copy), and live end-to-end predictions were verified against known feature values during manual testing.
assertions.evidence: Recorded honestly as not_run rather than claimed as pass - file-identity is a strong argument for parity but is not the same as an executed, repeatable test.

assertions.claim: Response latency measured against problem_spec's latency budget.
assertions.method: problem_spec.constraints.latency_budget = 'not latency-sensitive; a single prediction can take seconds'. Manual local testing (curl against the running service) observed sub-100ms responses for single predictions, well inside that budget.
assertions.evidence: No formal p50/p99 load test was run - single-operator, a-few-times-a-day traffic makes one not currently worth building.

assertions.claim: Rollback (reverting to a previous model version) was tested, not assumed.
assertions.method: Not run. There is exactly one model version (2026-09-23-logreg-v1) and no prior version to roll back to yet.
assertions.evidence: Recorded honestly - the mechanism (docker-compose rebuilds from whatever ml/05-production/artifacts/ contains at that commit, so `git revert` on that directory is the rollback path) has not been exercised.

assertions.claim: A shadow run against live traffic was completed before serving.
assertions.method: Not run - see decision no-shadow-or-canary-rollout for why this was deliberately skipped at this scale.

assertions.claim: The model artifact's SHA-256 was recorded at build time and is verified before every load.
assertions.method: Verified using the ml-kernel's own scripts/verify_artifact.py against the built artifact, and confirmed the service's own startup check (predictor/app/model.py) refuses to load on a deliberately corrupted hash file (tested manually: replaced model.sha256 with a wrong value, confirmed the service logs model_load_failed and /ready returns 503).
assertions.evidence: sha256 = d15dd7cd3f2315b97a59e380a281704f36e3cbbfa27e29b0de5bca8050565b72 (see ml/05-production/artifacts/model.sha256). verify_artifact.py confirms 'hash matches the expected value'.

assertions.claim: No secrets are baked into the predictor image or its config.
assertions.method: Manual review of predictor/Dockerfile, docker-compose.yml's predictor service block, and predictor/app/*.py - the service takes no credentials at all (it only loads a local model file and serves HTTP), so there is nothing to leak.

assertions.claim: Raw caption text is never written to logs.
assertions.method: Code review of predictor/app/main.py's logging call - it logs request_id, model_version, platform, label, probability, latency_ms only. The caption string itself never appears in any log statement.

assertions.claim: The endpoint is versioned and returns the model version in its response.
assertions.method: Route is dhaka-kacchi-connect's POST /v1/admin/post-predict (the /v1 prefix is this backend's existing API version, applied uniformly - not a new versioning scheme just for this feature); the predictor service's own response and the proxied admin response both include model_version.

assertions.claim: The full chain (admin frontend -> Node backend -> internal predictor service) was exercised live, not just unit-tested in isolation.
assertions.method: Ran all three pieces locally (predictor via its own isolated venv, the Node worker with PREDICTOR_URL pointed at it, the Vite frontend dev server), created a throwaway local-only admin test account, logged in through the real browser UI, submitted a real draft post through the /admin/post-predict form, and confirmed a real prediction rendered with plausible reasons. Deleted the throwaway test account afterward.
assertions.evidence: Live UI result: 'Likely below typical engagement', 47% confidence, top reasons is_video=True (+0.45), hashtag_count (-0.43), hour_bucket_evening (-0.31) - consistent with the coefficients reported in ml/03-modeling/report.md.

risks.description: The actual `docker compose build predictor` was never run in this session - no Docker daemon was available. Verification instead used an identical file layout (app/ + model/ directories matching the Dockerfile's COPY destinations exactly) run through the real predictor/.venv and a real uvicorn process, plus a full live click-through in the browser.
risks.mitigation: The first real deploy (git push to main, per this repo's existing CI/CD) will build the actual image for the first time. If it fails, the failure is caught by deploy.sh's own health-check gate before ordering-backend is touched (predictor's healthcheck blocks ordering-backend's depends_on), so a broken predictor build cannot silently break the live site - but this is still the first real test of the Dockerfile itself.

risks.description: Training/serving parity relies on features.py being copied verbatim at build time, not on an executed, repeatable test that would catch a future accidental divergence (e.g. someone editing the copy in predictor/ instead of the source in ml/03-modeling/).
risks.mitigation: The Dockerfile's own comment states the file must come from ml/03-modeling/features.py, not be hand-edited in place. A CI parity test is a reasonable future addition, not built this pass.

risks.description: Only structured stdout logs exist - no drift detection, no dashboard, no alerting.
risks.mitigation: Deliberately scoped to the project's actual size (single operator, low volume) rather than over-built. docker compose logs predictor is the real, available inspection path if something looks wrong.

risks.description: The is_video boolean is still one-hot encoded into two mirror-image columns in the shipped artifact (same issue noted in 03-modeling's risks) - harmless for a linear model but slightly wasteful.
risks.mitigation: Cosmetic; not worth a re-fit just for this. Fix (OneHotEncoder(drop='if_binary')) the next time the model is retrained for a real reason.

outputs.name: Predictor service

outputs.description: Sibling repo. POST /v1/admin/post-predict, proxies to the internal predictor service.

outputs.name: Admin frontend page
outputs.description: Sibling repo. Form + result display, wired into the admin nav.

next_stage_needs: First real push to main will build predictor/Dockerfile on the actual VPS for the first time - watch that deploy closely (docker compose logs predictor) rather than assuming the local-file-layout verification generalizes perfectly to the real Docker build.

Once real usage accumulates (the operator actually uses /admin/post-predict against real drafts), it's worth manually comparing a handful of predictions against what the post actually did after publishing - an informal, manual check on real-world calibration, not a formal monitoring pipeline.
Retraining is manual - re-run ml/00 through ml/03 (order matters) then ml/05-production/build_artifact.py once post volume has grown enough to matter (see ml/03-modeling's dl_gate.revisit_if).

serving_spec.serving_stack: FastAPI + uvicorn, internal-only docker-compose service (predictor/), proxied by dhaka-kacchi-connect's Node/Hono admin backend

monitoring.label_latency: hours to a few days (engagement accumulates after publishing)
monitoring.alerting: none automated - docker compose logs predictor is the manual inspection path

retraining.cadence: no fixed cadence - re-run when post volume has grown meaningfully, see ml/03-modeling's dl_gate.revisit_if
retraining.orchestrator: none - manual script sequence (ml/01-data/extract.py -> ml/03-modeling/train.py -> ml/05-production/build_artifact.py)
retraining.rollback: git revert on ml/05-production/artifacts/ + predictor/, then re-deploy via the existing CI/CD pipeline

rollout.notes: See decision no-shadow-or-canary-rollout for why - single internal operator, advisory-only, low volume.

governance.human_oversight: The operator reviews every prediction before deciding whether to act on it; the prediction has no automated effect on publishing or anything else.
governance.logging_retention: Container stdout logs only, retention governed by the VPS's own Docker logging driver defaults - not a formally configured retention policy.
